tagline: A road promised in wartime, finished half a century on.
intro: From Annette Bay, on the side of the island that faces Ketchikan, Walden Point Road runs 14.7 miles to Metlakatla. It keeps to the edge of the forest, looking out over the ocean. Waterfalls are many along the way, there are creeks where fish spawn, and Sitka black-tailed deer are a common sight on the muskeg side.
During the Second World War the United States promised the Metlakatla Indian Community a road across the island in exchange for an airfield. More than half a century later, military crews built it.

moments.title: Annette Bay
moments.text: The road begins here with views across to Ketchikan, and pullouts along the way give room to stop and look out over the water.

moments.title: Metlakatla
moments.text: Named for the British Columbia village that some 800 Tsimshian left by canoe with William Duncan in 1887, it is the main town of Alaska's only Indian reserve.

practical: Visitor, fishing and hunting permits come from the Metlakatla Indian Community.
